```{r}
#| include: false
source("assets/setup.R")
source("assets/quiz.R")
a_b   <- aov(bmi ~ wealth_index_of_participants, data = p)
a_tab <- summary(a_b)[[1]]
tk    <- TukeyHSD(a_b)$wealth_index_of_participants
eta   <- eta_squared(a_b)$Eta2
bm    <- p |> group_by(wealth_index_of_participants) |> summarise(m = mean(bmi))
kw    <- kruskal.test(sbp_presentation ~ marital_status_of_participants, data = p)
dn    <- dunn_test(p, sbp_presentation ~ marital_status_of_participants, p.adjust.method = "holm")
age_m <- tapply(p$age_of_participants, p$marital_status_of_participants, mean)
fbs_long <- p |> select(s_no, fbs_presentation, fbs_3_months, fbs_6_months) |>
  pivot_longer(-s_no, names_to = "time", values_to = "fbs") |>
  mutate(time = factor(time, c("fbs_presentation", "fbs_3_months", "fbs_6_months")))
rm_a  <- anova_test(data = fbs_long, dv = fbs, wid = s_no, within = time)
sbp_long <- p |> select(s_no, sbp_presentation, sbp_3_months, sbp_6_months) |>
  pivot_longer(-s_no, names_to = "time", values_to = "sbp") |>
  mutate(time = factor(time, c("sbp_presentation", "sbp_3_months", "sbp_6_months")))
fr    <- friedman_test(sbp_long, sbp ~ time | s_no)
kw_w  <- friedman_effsize(sbp_long, sbp ~ time | s_no)$effsize
ca    <- cor.test(p$age_of_participants, p$sbp_in_mm_hg)
cs    <- cor.test(p$age_of_participants, p$glucose_level_mg_d_l, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Session 4: two groups, or two measurements on the same people
- Today: **three or more** groups or time points, the **relationship** between two numbers, and putting it all into **words**
- By the end you can:
  - run ANOVA or Kruskal–Wallis, and their **post hoc** tests, only when they are warranted
  - check **sphericity** for repeated measures and use **paired** post hoc tests
  - read **r**, its CI and **r²**, and choose Pearson or Spearman
  - control for **multiple testing**, and write a results paragraph
:::

# Topic 1 — Three or more independent groups {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## One-way ANOVA: BMI by wealth index

```{r}
p |> group_by(wealth_index_of_participants) |> summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(bmi), sd = sd(bmi))
a_b <- aov(bmi ~ wealth_index_of_participants, data = p)
summary(a_b)
```

## Check the assumptions on the residuals

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 4.6
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| echo: false
ggplot(tibble(r = residuals(a_b)), aes(sample = r)) + stat_qq(colour = col_blue, alpha = .5) +
  stat_qq_line(colour = col_red) + labs(x = "Normal quantiles", y = "Residuals (kg/m²)")
```
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
leveneTest(bmi ~ wealth_index_of_participants, data = p)
oneway.test(bmi ~ wealth_index_of_participants, data = p)$p.value   # Welch ANOVA
```
:::
:::

- Residuals on the line; Levene `r fp(leveneTest(bmi ~ wealth_index_of_participants, data = p)[1, 3])`, but the SDs differ little (largest under 1.5 × smallest) and **Welch ANOVA** agrees (`r fp(oneway.test(bmi ~ wealth_index_of_participants, data = p)$p.value)`): the conclusion does not depend on the choice

## Significant: now how big, and where?

::: {.eq}
"Mean BMI rose with household wealth, from `r f(bm$m[1])` kg/m² in the poorest to `r f(bm$m[5])` kg/m² in the richest group (one-way ANOVA, F(`r a_tab$Df[1]`, `r a_tab$Df[2]`) = `r f(a_tab$"F value"[1], 1)`, `r fp(a_tab$"Pr(>F)"[1])`; η² = `r f(eta, 2)`). Richest vs poorest: `r f(tk["richest-poorest", "diff"])` kg/m² (95% CI `r f(tk["richest-poorest", "lwr"])` to `r f(tk["richest-poorest", "upr"])`, Tukey)."
:::

::: {.incremental}
- The F-test says only "the means are not all equal"; **Tukey** gives each pair's difference with a CI adjusted for `r nrow(tk)` comparisons
- η² = `r f(eta, 2)`: wealth explains about **`r f(100 * eta, 0)`%** of the variation in BMI, a **medium** effect (0.01 small, 0.06 medium, 0.14 large); most variation is between people within a group
- The groups are **ordered**: a trend test or regression with wealth as a score (Regression track) uses that order and asks one question instead of `r nrow(tk)`
:::

## Post hoc tests: when and which

| After | Post hoc | R |
|---|---|---|
| One-way ANOVA, equal SDs | **Tukey HSD** | `TukeyHSD(aov(...))` |
| Welch ANOVA, unequal SDs | **Games–Howell** | `rstatix::games_howell_test()` |
| Kruskal–Wallis | **Dunn** with Holm adjustment | `rstatix::dunn_test(..., p.adjust.method = "holm")` |

::: {.warn}
Run post hoc tests to answer a question you **planned**, or after a clear overall result. Hunting through every pair after a non-significant overall test produces false findings.
:::

## Kruskal–Wallis: systolic pressure by marital status

```{r}
p |> group_by(marital_status_of_participants) |>
  summarise(median = median(sbp_presentation), q1 = quantile(sbp_presentation, .25), q3 = quantile(sbp_presentation, .75))
kruskal.test(sbp_presentation ~ marital_status_of_participants, data = p)
```

- For skewed outcomes or outliers (SBP at presentation is right-skewed); compares the **distributions**, through ranks
- `r fp(kw$p.value)`: a difference somewhere. **Dunn** (Holm-adjusted) shows where: formerly married vs never married `r fp(dn$p.adj[2])`, vs currently married `r fp(dn$p.adj[3])`

## Before you explain it: who is in each group?

```{r}
dunn_test(p, sbp_presentation ~ marital_status_of_participants, p.adjust.method = "holm") |>
  select(group1, group2, p.adj)
```

::: {.warn}
Formerly married adults (mostly widowed) are **older**: mean age `r f(age_m[3])` vs `r f(age_m[2])` (currently) and `r f(age_m[1])` years (never married), and SBP rises with age. The test shows a **difference**, not its **cause**: separating marital status from age needs **regression** (Regression track).
:::

# Topic 2 — Repeated measurements {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Repeated-measures ANOVA: fasting glucose at 0, 3 and 6 months

```{r}
fbs_long <- p |> select(s_no, fbs_presentation, fbs_3_months, fbs_6_months) |>
  pivot_longer(-s_no, names_to = "time", values_to = "fbs")
anova_test(data = fbs_long, dv = fbs, wid = s_no, within = time)
```

## Sphericity, and the correction {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
- **Sphericity**: the variance of the differences is the same for every pair of time points (0–3, 0–6, 3–6)
- **Mauchly's test** checks it; when violated, use the **Greenhouse–Geisser** corrected p-value (`p[GG]`), which `anova_test()` prints alongside
- Here Mauchly `r fp(rm_a$"Mauchly's Test for Sphericity"$p)`: sphericity is violated (the 0–6 month changes vary more than the 0–3), so report the **GG-corrected** result, ε = `r f(rm_a$"Sphericity Corrections"$GGe, 2)`
- **ges** (generalised η²) = `r f(rm_a$ANOVA$ges, 2)`: a **modest** share of the total variation, because people differ from **each other** far more than from one visit to the next. The F-test is huge because each person is compared with themselves
:::

::: {.eq}
"Mean fasting glucose fell from `r f(mean(p$fbs_presentation))` mg/dL at presentation to `r f(mean(p$fbs_3_months))` at 3 and `r f(mean(p$fbs_6_months))` at 6 months (repeated-measures ANOVA with Greenhouse–Geisser correction, F(`r f(rm_a$ANOVA$DFn * rm_a$"Sphericity Corrections"$GGe, 2)`, `r f(rm_a$ANOVA$DFd * rm_a$"Sphericity Corrections"$GGe, 0)`) = `r f(rm_a$ANOVA$F, 0)`, `r fp(rm_a$"Sphericity Corrections"$"p[GG]")`; generalised η² = `r f(rm_a$ANOVA$ges, 2)`)."
:::

## Post hoc for repeated measures must be **paired**

```{r}
pairwise.t.test(fbs_long$fbs, fbs_long$time, paired = TRUE, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
```

::: {.warn}
Without `paired = TRUE`, `pairwise.t.test()` treats the three visits as **independent groups** of different people and pools their SD: the wrong test for repeated measurements. Because the visits are strongly correlated it throws away most of the information: its p-values are many orders of magnitude larger, and with a smaller change it would miss it altogether.
:::

## Friedman: systolic pressure at 0, 3 and 6 months

```{r}
sbp_long <- p |> select(s_no, sbp_presentation, sbp_3_months, sbp_6_months) |>
  pivot_longer(-s_no, names_to = "time", values_to = "sbp")
friedman.test(sbp ~ time | s_no, data = sbp_long)
pairwise.wilcox.test(sbp_long$sbp, sbp_long$time, paired = TRUE, p.adjust.method = "holm")$p.value
```

- The rank-based partner of repeated-measures ANOVA; every person needs **all** time points
- Medians `r median(p$sbp_presentation)` → `r median(p$sbp_3_months)` → `r median(p$sbp_6_months)` mmHg; effect size **Kendall's W** = `r f(kw_w, 2)` (0.1 small, 0.3 moderate, 0.5 large)

# Topic 3 — Two numbers together: correlation {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Plot first, then r

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(p, aes(age_of_participants, sbp_in_mm_hg)) + geom_point(alpha = .35, colour = col_blue) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = col_red) + labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "SBP (mmHg)")
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r}
cor.test(p$age_of_participants, p$sbp_in_mm_hg)
```
:::
:::

## Reading r

::: {.eq}
"Systolic pressure rose with age (Pearson r = `r f(ca$estimate, 2)`, 95% CI `r f(ca$conf.int[1], 2)` to `r f(ca$conf.int[2], 2)`; `r fp(ca$p.value)`)."
:::

::: {.incremental}
- **r²** = `r f(ca$estimate^2, 2)`: age accounts for about **`r f(100 * ca$estimate^2, 0)`%** of the variation in SBP. A **moderate** association: highly significant, yet most of the variation lies elsewhere
- Correlation measures **linear association** only; it is not agreement (use Bland–Altman for that) and not causation
- To estimate *how much* SBP changes per year of age, and to adjust for other factors: **regression** (Regression track)
:::

## Pearson or Spearman?

| | Pearson r | Spearman ρ |
|---|---|---|
| Measures | **linear** association | **monotonic** association (through ranks) |
| Needs | roughly normal pairs, no extreme outliers | ordinal or numeric data, any shape |
| Use for | age and SBP | glucose (skewed, outliers up to `r max(p$glucose_level_mg_d_l)` mg/dL), ordinal scores |

```{r}
cor.test(p$age_of_participants, p$glucose_level_mg_d_l, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$estimate
```

# Topic 4 — Many tests, and the write-up {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Multiple testing

::: {.incremental}
- At p < 0.05, **1 in 20** tests of a true null hypothesis comes out "significant" by chance
- 20 independent comparisons → about a **64%** chance of at least one false positive
- **Bonferroni**: multiply each p by the number of tests (simple, strict). **Holm**: the same idea step by step, never worse, usually better
- `p.adjust(c(0.01, 0.02, 0.04), method = "holm")` → `r paste(signif(p.adjust(c(0.01, 0.02, 0.04), method = "holm"), 2), collapse = ", ")`
- Decide the **main** comparisons in advance; label the rest as **exploratory**
:::

## A results paragraph

::: {.eq}
"Of `r nrow(p)` adults, `r sum(p$past_history_of_diabetes == "yes")` (`r f(100 * mean(p$past_history_of_diabetes == "yes"))`%) reported diabetes. They were older (mean difference `r f(diff(t.test(age_of_participants ~ past_history_of_diabetes, data = p)$estimate))` years, 95% CI `r f(-t.test(age_of_participants ~ past_history_of_diabetes, data = p)$conf.int[2])` to `r f(-t.test(age_of_participants ~ past_history_of_diabetes, data = p)$conf.int[1])`; Welch t-test) and more often hypertensive (odds ratio `r f(fisher.test(table(p$past_history_of_hypertension, p$past_history_of_diabetes))$estimate)`, 95% CI `r f(fisher.test(table(p$past_history_of_hypertension, p$past_history_of_diabetes))$conf.int[1])` to `r f(fisher.test(table(p$past_history_of_hypertension, p$past_history_of_diabetes))$conf.int[2])`; Fisher's exact test). Mean fasting glucose fell over six months (Topic 2)."
:::

- **Every** claim: the numbers, the **effect with its CI**, the **test**; p-values to 2–3 decimals, "p < 0.001" below that
- Methods: how assumptions were checked and what was done when they failed (Session 2)

## Reporting checklist

| | Write down |
|---|---|
| Descriptives | n for every group; mean (SD) or median (IQR); n (%) |
| Data checks | what was excluded and why; sensitivity analysis |
| Assumptions | how checked (plots, tests); what was done if not met |
| Each result | effect size **with 95% CI**, the test, the exact p |
| Many tests | which were planned; the adjustment method |
| Interpretation | size and importance, not only "significant"; association, not cause |

Building Table 1 with **gtsummary**: [which of these tests it runs, which it cannot, and a pipeline that picks each test](../gtsummary/gtsummary_tutorial.qmd#which-tests-gtsummary-can-run-and-which-it-cannot)

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("t5q1", "A one-way ANOVA gives p = 0.056 and eta squared = 0.009. What is the best reading?",
         c("A trend that would be significant with a few more people",
           "Weak evidence, and the grouping explains under 1% of variation",
           "Clear evidence of a difference, since p is close to 0.05",
           "The groups are now proven equal, so no differences are reported"), answer = 2,
         explain = "p = 0.056 is weak evidence, not a 'trend'; eta squared below 0.01 means the grouping explains almost none of the variation. Report the group means and the CIs.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("t5q2", "Fasting glucose was measured in the same adults at 0, 3 and 6 months. Which post hoc comparison is right after a repeated-measures ANOVA?",
         c("pairwise.t.test() with the default settings on the long data",
           "pairwise.t.test() with paired = TRUE and an adjustment",
           "Three separate Welch t-tests with no multiplicity adjustment",
           "A Tukey HSD test on the aov() of glucose by time point only"), answer = 2,
         explain = "The same people appear at every time point, so the comparisons must be paired, with a correction (Bonferroni or Holm) for the three tests.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("t5q3", "Mauchly's test for a repeated-measures ANOVA gives p = 0.002. What should you report?",
         c("The uncorrected F-test, since sphericity is a minor point",
           "A Kruskal-Wallis test in place of the repeated measures model",
           "The Greenhouse-Geisser corrected p-value for the time effect",
           "Nothing, as the analysis cannot be done with these data"), answer = 3,
         explain = "A small Mauchly p means sphericity is violated. The Greenhouse-Geisser correction adjusts the degrees of freedom; anova_test() prints it as p[GG].")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("t5q4", paste0("Age and systolic pressure: r = ", f(ca$estimate, 2), ", 95% CI ", f(ca$conf.int[1], 2), " to ", f(ca$conf.int[2], 2), ", ", fp(ca$p.value), ". What is the right reading?"),
         c("A strong link, since the p-value is so very small",
           paste0("Age explains about ", f(100 * ca$estimate^2, 0), "% of the variation in SBP"),
           "Getting older causes a rise in systolic pressure",
           "SBP and age agree closely when measured in adults"), answer = 2,
         explain = paste0("r squared = ", f(ca$estimate^2, 2), ": a real, moderate association; most of the variation in SBP lies elsewhere. A small p reflects the large sample, not strength. Correlation is neither causation nor agreement."))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_fill("t5q5", "With 20 independent tests at the 5% level and every null hypothesis true, the chance of at least one false positive is about what percent? (number only)",
          accept = c("64", "64%", "0.64", "65", "64.2"),
          explain = "1 - 0.95^20 = 0.64. Plan the main comparisons, adjust (Holm or Bonferroni), and label the rest as exploratory.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- ≥ 3 groups: ANOVA (Welch if SDs differ) or **Kruskal–Wallis**; post hoc only when warranted
- Repeated measures: check **sphericity**; post hoc tests must be **paired**
- Correlation: **plot**, then r with its CI; r² for strength; not cause, not agreement
- Plan the main tests; **adjust** the rest; report effect sizes with CIs, in sentences
:::
